conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Linda Williams from the IRS Tax Refund Department. Am I speaking with Mr. Carter?
Yes, that's me. Sorry, I've got a lot going on, can we make this quick?
Absolutely, sir. The reason for my call is regarding your recent federal tax return. Our system has flagged you as eligible for a special stimulus refund of $1,750.
Oh, really? I didn't think I was getting anything back this year.

I understand your surprise. The IRS is issuing additional payments to qualified individuals, and you're on the list. However, before we can release your refund, there's a mandatory identity verification and processing fee of $89.
Wait, I have to pay to get my refund? That doesn't sound right.

Due to increased fraud during tax season, the IRS now requires a small clearance fee to verify your identity and process the payment. It's a one-time step, and once it's completed, your refund will be deposited within 24 hours.
I really don't have much time, I have to pick up my daughter soon. Is there any way around this?
Unfortunately, if the fee isn't paid by 5 p.m. today, the refund will be marked as unclaimed, and you may have to wait until next tax year to apply again.
That would be awful. I could really use the money right now. How do I pay the fee?
To expedite the process, we accept Zelle or Cash App payments. I can provide you with our Treasury processing handle, or if you prefer, you can use a debit or credit card over the phone.
I guess I could try Zelle. What's the handle?
Please send the $89 fee to irs-clearance@usa-gov.com via Zelle. Once you're done, let me know and I'll confirm the payment in our system.
Okay, I'll have to move some money first. Can you hold for a second?
Of course. While you do that, please have your tax file number ready in case I need to confirm your details.
Alright. I'm transferring it now. Done. Should I send a screenshot?
No need for a screenshot, our system logs the transfer automatically. Just to confirm, did you send it to irs-clearance@usa-gov.com?
Yes, that's where it went.
Perfect. I see the payment is pending. For security, I'll need to confirm your bank account where the refund should be deposited. Can you provide your routing and account number?
I'd rather not give that over the phone. Is there another way?
If you prefer, you can provide a debit card number, or I can reserve your refund check for pickup at your local IRS office. However, that might take several weeks.
No, I can't wait that long. I guess I'll give you my debit card.
Thank you. Please read the 16-digit number on the front of your card, expiration date, and the three digits on the back.
Alright, it's 4567 8910 2345 6789, expiration 10/29, and 321 on the back.

Thank you, Mr. Carter. I'm processing your refund request now. If there are any discrepancies, the IRS may place a hold on your account, which could delay not only this refund but also future tax filings.
Oh, I hope that doesn't happen. I really need this refund.
As long as you followed instructions, there shouldn't be any issues. You'll receive an email confirmation shortly. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that's it. Thanks, I guess.
Thank you for your cooperation. Have a good day, Mr. Carter.
